MAIN.description:
I am a computer science graduate with hands-on experience in mobile, web, backend, and database systems development.
In my free time I like developing my own hobby projects to learn new technologies. I am particularly interested in writing Google extensions and mobile applications.

MICROSOFT.meta_title: Search Automatic Rewards: daily Bing searches for Microsoft Rewards
MICROSOFT.meta_description: Free browser extension for Chrome and Firefox that runs your daily Bing searches for Microsoft Rewards and opens your daily set, once a day.
MICROSOFT.tagline: Runs your daily Bing searches for Microsoft Rewards, once a day, in the background.
MICROSOFT.intro: Microsoft Rewards gives points for searching on Bing every day. Search Automatic Rewards does those searches for you: once a day it opens Bing searches in background tabs, closes them again, and goes through the daily set on your Rewards dashboard.
MICROSOFT.risk: Use at your own risk. Microsoft's Rewards terms prohibit bots and automated searches, and Microsoft can limit or suspend accounts and void points. The extension only opens Bing searches in your own browser, but that doesn't make it allowed.
MICROSOFT.step1: Join Microsoft Rewards and sign in to your Microsoft account on bing.com, in the browser profile where you installed the extension.
MICROSOFT.step2: Open the popup and set your account level (Member, Silver or Gold). It decides how many searches to run, or you can enter a number yourself.
MICROSOFT.step3: If the daily set doesn't open its tasks, allow pop-ups on rewards.bing.com in your browser's site settings.
MICROSOFT.step4: That's all. It runs once a day when you start the browser, or within a few hours if the browser stays open. Press Get rewards to run it now.
MICROSOFT.feature1: Daily searches: 5, 10 or 20 Bing searches depending on your account level, or any number from 1 to 999. Each one opens in a background tab and closes a few seconds after it loads.
MICROSOFT.feature2: Natural search terms: searches are everyday phrases built from built-in word lists, not random letters.
MICROSOFT.feature3: Randomized timing: searches are about a minute apart by default, with random variation. You can change the delay, but below 30 seconds Microsoft often stops crediting searches.
MICROSOFT.feature4: Daily set: opens the Rewards dashboard, clicks through the daily set and takes you back to the tab you were on.
MICROSOFT.feature5: Once a day, automatically: runs when the browser starts and checks again every few hours if it stays open. If you're signed in to the same browser account on several computers, it runs on only one of them each day.
MICROSOFT.feature6: Optional extras: claim points waiting on the dashboard, and open the first result in each search tab. Both are off by default.
MICROSOFT.feature7: Progress at a glance: a progress bar in the popup and a count on the toolbar icon. Stop searches ends a run early.
MICROSOFT.popup_caption: The popup: run now, and choose what it does each day.
MICROSOFT.a1: No. Microsoft's Rewards terms prohibit automated searches, and accounts can be limited or suspended. The extension opens searches in your own browser as you would, but that doesn't make it allowed. Decide for yourself whether to take that risk.
MICROSOFT.q2: Why didn't some searches earn points?
MICROSOFT.a2: Microsoft decides which searches it credits. Searches less than 30 seconds apart often aren't credited, so keep the delay at 30 seconds or more. Also check that you're signed in on bing.com in this browser.
MICROSOFT.a3: No. It has no analytics and no server, keeps its settings in your browser and only opens Bing and Microsoft Rewards pages. It asks for access to Bing searches and rewards.bing.com, nothing else.
MICROSOFT.q4: Is there a version for Microsoft Edge?
MICROSOFT.a4: Not on Edge Add-ons, but Edge can install the Chrome version: open the Chrome Web Store link at the top of this page and allow extensions from other stores when Edge asks.
MICROSOFT.test_description: Mobile app for automating Microsoft Rewards points generation. It opens Bing tabs inside the app.

PROLIFIC.meta_title: Prolific Studies Notifier: instant alerts for new Prolific studies
PROLIFIC.meta_description: Free browser extension for Chrome and Firefox that plays a sound and shows a desktop notification the moment a new study appears on Prolific. Notify-only: it never joins or reserves studies.
PROLIFIC.tagline: A sound and a desktop notification the moment a new study appears on Prolific.
PROLIFIC.intro: Well-paid studies fill up within minutes. Prolific Studies Notifier watches the Prolific tab you have open and alerts you as soon as something new shows up, so you don't have to keep refreshing. It only notifies you: it never joins or reserves a study for you.
PROLIFIC.promo_alt: A desktop notification for a new Prolific study next to the extension's list of studies
PROLIFIC.setup_intro: If you just installed the extension, do this once:
PROLIFIC.step1: Open app.prolific.com/studies, log in and leave the tab open. It can stay in the background, and one tab is enough.
PROLIFIC.step2: Click the extension's icon and press Test. You should hear the alert sound and see a sample notification.
PROLIFIC.step3: No notification? Allow notifications for your browser in your operating system (Windows: Settings → System → Notifications; macOS: System Settings → Notifications), and turn off Focus or Do Not Disturb.
PROLIFIC.step4: Keep the browser open and the computer awake. A new study is picked up when Prolific refreshes its list, about every two minutes, or sooner with fast mode.
PROLIFIC.feature1: Sound and desktop alerts: six alert sounds with a volume slider, and a notification with the study's title, researcher, reward, hourly rate and duration. Clicking the notification opens the study.
PROLIFIC.feature2: Filters: only get alerts for studies above a minimum reward, hourly rate or duration, and skip studies with certain words in their name or researcher.
PROLIFIC.feature3: One alert per study: you aren't alerted again for a study you've already seen, even when Prolific lists many at once.
PROLIFIC.feature4: Studies list: every study you were alerted to, with search, sorting, a list or card layout, saved studies, CSV export and a full-page view.
PROLIFIC.feature5: Reliable in the background: stops the browser from putting your Prolific tab to sleep, and reloads it if Prolific stops refreshing.
PROLIFIC.feature6: Fast mode (optional): checks Prolific every 60 seconds, or at an interval you set, instead of waiting for its refresh. It's unofficial and off by default. If Prolific limits your account, fast mode pauses itself and tells you.
PROLIFIC.feature7: Open Prolific on startup: optionally opens the studies page when your browser starts, so you never forget to.
PROLIFIC.settings_caption: Settings: alert sound and volume, desktop notifications, fast mode and repeat alerts.
PROLIFIC.studies_caption: Studies tab: every study you were alerted to, with pay, hourly rate, duration and places left.
PROLIFIC.privacy1: It only runs on app.prolific.com, where it reads the list of studies. It never reads your login details.
PROLIFIC.privacy2: There are no analytics and no servers. Settings are kept in your browser's storage (and synced with your browser account if you use sync); the list of studies stays on this computer.
PROLIFIC.privacy3: Permissions: storage for settings, notifications for alerts and access to app.prolific.com. In Chrome, an offscreen page plays the alert sound.
PROLIFIC.privacy4: It's free, with no ads or paid features. The source code is on GitHub.
PROLIFIC.q1: Does it join or reserve studies for me?
PROLIFIC.a1: No. It only notifies you. You open the study and take part yourself.
PROLIFIC.a2: Press Test in the popup. If you hear the sound but see no notification, your operating system is blocking it: allow your browser in the notification settings and turn off Focus or Do Not Disturb. Also check that a logged-in app.prolific.com/studies tab is open.
PROLIFIC.q3: Does it work on my phone?
PROLIFIC.a3: No. It's an extension for desktop browsers, so your computer has to be on with the browser open.
PROLIFIC.q4: Is fast mode safe to use?
PROLIFIC.a4: Fast mode is unofficial: it asks Prolific for the list of studies more often than the site does by itself. It's off by default. If Prolific restricts or rate-limits your account, fast mode pauses for 30 to 60 minutes and shows a notification. Use it at your own risk.
PROLIFIC.q5: Why are the reward filters in pounds?
PROLIFIC.a5: Most Prolific studies pay in pounds. Studies paid in dollars are converted at a fixed rate ($1 = £0.80), so filters can be slightly off for them.
PROLIFIC.q6: Is there a version for Microsoft Edge?
PROLIFIC.a6: Not on Edge Add-ons yet, but Edge can install the Chrome version: open the Chrome Web Store link at the top of this page and allow extensions from other stores when Edge asks.

CLAIMER.meta_title: Free Game Claimer: auto claim free Epic, Steam, GOG & Prime games
CLAIMER.meta_description: Free browser extension that claims free games from Epic Games, Steam, GOG, IndieGala and Prime Gaming automatically, using the store accounts you're already logged into. Open source, for Chrome and Firefox.
CLAIMER.tagline: Claims free games from Epic Games, Steam, GOG, IndieGala and Prime Gaming for you, on a schedule you choose.
CLAIMER.intro: Stores give games away every week, but only to people who claim them in time. Free Game Claimer checks the stores you pick and claims each giveaway with the accounts you're already logged into in your browser. It never asks for your passwords.
CLAIMER.promo_alt: Free Game Claimer popup listing this week's free games from Epic Games and Prime Gaming
CLAIMER.step1: Add the extension to Chrome or Firefox (version 113 or newer) with the buttons at the top of this page.
CLAIMER.step2: Stay logged in to the stores you want games from, in the same browser. Right after installing, it checks Epic Games and Steam and claims anything that's free, in background tabs that close by themselves.
CLAIMER.step3: Open the popup to choose your stores and when to check. Turning on GOG, IndieGala or Prime Gaming asks you to allow access to those sites.
CLAIMER.step4: Pin the extension to the toolbar if you like. Its badge shows when it's claiming and when a store needs you.
CLAIMER.settings_caption: Settings: pause auto-claim, pick when it checks, set a minimum Steam rating and see which stores you're logged in to.
CLAIMER.feature1: Five stores: Epic Games and Steam are on by default. GOG, IndieGala and Prime Gaming are a click away.
CLAIMER.feature2: Your schedule: check on browser start, every hour, every 6 or 12 hours, or once a day at the hour you pick (the default is once a day). The Auto-claim switch pauses it, and Claim now checks right away.
CLAIMER.feature3: Free Games tab: every game that's free right now in your stores, when each giveaway ends, next week's Epic game, and an In library mark on games you already own on Steam or Epic.
CLAIMER.feature4: Steam rating filter: skip free Steam games rated below a level you choose, from 20%+ to 90%+ positive reviews.
CLAIMER.feature5: Prime Gaming: choose which offers to claim: Amazon Games, or games and codes for Epic, GOG, Microsoft Store and Legacy Games. Codes for GOG, Microsoft Store and Legacy Games are redeemed for you. Needs Amazon Prime.
CLAIMER.feature6: IndieGala: claims freebies and spins the daily Wheel of Fortune. A Steam key it wins is activated on your Steam account.
CLAIMER.feature7: No lost codes: a code or Steam key that can't be redeemed automatically, for example a region-locked key, waits in a Needs manual redeem list with a Copy button.
CLAIMER.feature8: Store status: the popup shows whether you're logged in to each store, and tells you when a store needs a captcha or has changed in a way the extension can't handle yet.
CLAIMER.library_caption: Free Games tab: when each giveaway ends, games already in your library and next week's free game.
CLAIMER.privacy1: It uses the store accounts you're logged into in this browser. It never asks for your passwords and doesn't store them.
CLAIMER.privacy2: There is no account, server, analytics or tracking. Settings and game lists stay in your browser's extension storage, and the extension only talks to the stores.
CLAIMER.privacy3: At install it asks for access to Steam and Epic Games. Access to GOG, IndieGala and the Prime Gaming sites (Amazon, plus the GOG, Microsoft and Legacy Games redeem pages) is only requested when you turn that store on.
CLAIMER.privacy4: It's free, with no ads or paid features, and open source under the GPL-3.0 licence. Read the code on GitHub.
CLAIMER.q1: Why didn't it claim a game?
CLAIMER.a1: Open the popup and check the store's status. The usual reasons: you're logged out of that store, Epic is showing a captcha (its tab is brought to the front for you to solve), the store is switched off, or the Steam rating filter skipped the game. Claim now tries again right away.
CLAIMER.q2: Which Steam games does it claim?
CLAIMER.a2: Paid games that are temporarily 100% off. Free-to-play games aren't giveaways, so it leaves them alone.
CLAIMER.q3: Does it work with Prime Gaming?
CLAIMER.a3: Yes, with an Amazon account that has Prime. Turn Prime Gaming on and tick the offers you want. If an offer needs an Epic or GOG account you haven't linked to Amazon yet, Amazon's linking page is left open for you.
CLAIMER.q4: How often does it check for free games?
CLAIMER.a4: As often as you choose: on browser start, every hour, every 6 or 12 hours, or once a day, which is the default. For the daily check you can pick an hour; if your browser is closed then, it runs when you next open it that day.
CLAIMER.q5: Does it claim Epic's holiday mystery games?
CLAIMER.a5: It claims every game that Epic's free games list shows as free, on your schedule. It has no special handling for the mystery games, so if one is missed, press Claim now or claim it on Epic's site.
CLAIMER.a6: Yes. It has no ads, no paid tier and no premium features, and the code is open source. If it saves you money, you can support it below, but you never have to.
CLAIMER.q7: Is there a version for Microsoft Edge?
CLAIMER.a7: Not on Edge Add-ons yet, but Edge can install the Chrome version: open the Chrome Web Store link at the top of this page and allow extensions from other stores when Edge asks.
